text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak discusses with Somali faction leaders Hussein Aideed and Ali Mahdi Mohamed the agreement they reached to solve the crisis in Somalia. Mahdi tells reporters after the meeting that he agreed with Aideed to end divisions in Mogadishu.
- Mubarak and United Arab Emirates President, Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan, discuss the results of the Sharm el-Sheikh Mideast peace meeting over the telephone.
- European Union envoy Miguel Moratinos arrives in Cairo on Tuesday for talks on the Middle East peace process.
- Egypt's first lady Suzanne Mubarak donates two libraries to the childern of Gaza and Mallawi.

- Egypt's ambassador to Israel says that there is an Israeli conviction that Egypt is the key to Middle East peace because it is the only country that honestly tells Israel what it thinks and what can be done and what is impossible.
- Presidential advisor Osama el-Baz gives Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu the Palestinian response to his suggestions.

- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi will sign in the next few days four oil and gas exploration agreements in the Gulf of Suez, the Western Desert and Beni Suef. Fourteen new wells will be drilled at a total cost of $39 million.
- Our ambassador to Israel says Egypt will not accept a fait accompli in Jerusalem. Palestinian anger at the Israeli plan to usurp Jerusalem and 60 percent of West Bank lands.
- A new Boeing 777 plane delivered to EgyptAir.
